🚨 FORECLOSURE WATCH // Bank repossessions jumped 42% in August 🏠

Lenders repossessed 5,794 homes in August, up 42% from a year earlier and up 22% from July, according to ATTOM. Texas accounted for nearly a third of them.

 * 🏠 Completed repossessions: 5,794, up 42% YoY, up 22% MoM
 * 🤠 Texas: 1,835, the most of any state (California next at 589)
 * 🏙️ Houston 448, Dallas 402, San Antonio 256 led all metros
 * 📋 Total filings: 40,277, up 13% YoY
 * 📉 New starts: 25,894, up just 7% YoY

▬▬▬

⚠️ THE CATCH
Completed foreclosures are a lagging indicator, marking the end of a process that started months or years ago, while new starts grew only 7%. ATTOM notes total activity remains below pre-pandemic norms, so this is a surge from a low base, not a 2008 replay. The data is August's, released weeks ago and repackaged in today's headlines.

▬▬▬

🧠 THE TAKEAWAY
The distress is real but concentrated: three Texas metros drove nearly a fifth of all repossessions. The number to watch is new starts, and those are barely growing. Are banks working through old backlog, or is fresh distress building? 👇 NFA

I’ve spent 30+ years researching the phenomenon, made multiple documentaries, and I’m an experiencer myself. I’m not closed to non-human intelligence. But “reptilian aliens” is pure cultural projection with zero evolutionary grounding.
If biological aliens exist and evolved under natural selection (the only process we know produces complex life), why would they look like Earth’s reptiles?
Reptiles are a specific Earth lineage — amniotes with scales that evolved for water retention on land, often ectothermic. Complex intelligence on Earth arose in high-metabolism endotherms (mammals, birds) that can fuel big brains. There’s no reason an alien biosphere would converge on “cold-blooded, scaly, bipedal humanoid with claws.”
Convergent evolution is real (eyes, wings, streamlined swimmers have evolved independently many times because physics and ecology constrain solutions). We might expect bilateral symmetry, sensory organs, manipulators for technology. We should not expect Earth’s taxonomic labels. A full reptilian humanoid is double anthropocentrism: humanoid body plan + our mythical/sci-fi “lizard people” overlay (Icke, pulp fiction, Hollywood).
Grusch himself stresses he never saw them — this is colleague hearsay, no evidence, no bodies, no DNA, nothing. It fits decades of unverified crash-retrieval lore far better than any biology or physics we understand. Official reviews (AARO etc.) have found nothing supporting these claims.
The real phenomenon — whatever it is — is strange enough without us forcing it into cartoon reptiles. Let’s demand actual evidence, not folklore.
What do you think — is the reptilian idea just our ancient serpent myths projected onto the sky?
